articles.summary: UnitedHealthcare and Cigna have both said in writing that what you bill for maternity in January depends on a CMS final rule expected in November. Meanwhile Highmark started transitioning on October 1 keyed to the due date, and Aetna started September 1 keyed to how many prenatal visits a patient has had this year. Four large payers, four different tests, for the same patient in the same month.
articles.title: Two of the largest payers have tied January billing to a rule CMS has not written yet

articles.summary: Our maternity billing resource tracks over 3000 health plans. 181 have confirmed how they are moving off global maternity billing. Of the 127 that committed to a date, 96 have already taken effect. Only 31 land on January 1, 2027. The transition most teams are planning for is mostly behind them.
articles.title: Three quarters of the confirmed maternity billing changes have already happened (and 90% of payers haven't even announced yet)

articles.summary: For the last few months, we've been tracking the maternity billings that are underway through the beginning of the year. Our goal overall has been to help our clients and the women's health community and RCN community at large to understand what changes are coming down the line and proactively respond. We ensure that their internal billing rules and SOPs are able to be updated in real time in line with payer changes. Overall, that research is here: https://www.substrateai.com/payers/2027-substrate-maternity-resource-center‍ We'll be updating it continuously as we learn more from payers and learn more from practices. We have folks on our team manually reviewing each policy as we see the updates coming in.
articles.title: 9 ways payers are moving off global maternity billing (and which one your patients fall under)

articles.summary: Of 50 states and DC, only nine have a confirmed 2027 maternity billing transition from a Medicaid-named plan. Forty have no Medicaid policy record at all. Medicaid pays for roughly four in ten births nationally, which makes this the largest blind spot in the whole transition.
articles.title: Medicaid covers four in ten births. We have confirmed 2027 guidance in nine states.

articles.summary: If you bill for maternity care, the way you get paid is about to change. Starting January 1, 2027, the American Medical Association is deleting the global code for maternity billing and moving to a CPT and modifier based approach. This affects essentially everyone who bills maternity: hospitals with maternity departments, women's health clinics, and OBGYN practices.
articles.title: The Maternity Global Is Going Away: What the 2027 CPT Change Means for Your Billing
